thread:
jordan: FYI - I hit a regression on Mistral-7B when sequence_len crosses ~2k in sliding-window workloads. Latency jumps ~30% and kernel chooser switches to a fallback path. repro steps + perf numbers below.
meera: ugh. do you have a short perf diff and kernel logs? can we pin to the fast kernel for now?
sam: pinging kernel-chooser folks. if it's selecting fallback we might be misclassifying RoPE scale/seq bound. logs?
jordan: pasted run log (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17 09:12:01] seq_len=2048 batch=1 kernel=matmul_fp16_fast latency=8.6ms
[2026-03-17 09:12:12] seq_len=2056 batch=1 kernel=matmul_generic latency=11.3ms
chooser: reason=tile_overflow pos_wrap_detected=true rope_scale=1.0
```
jordan: note chooser flagged pos_wrap_detected=true and switched to generic matmul + slower KV gather path.
carla: is pos_wrap actually happening or false-positive? Mistral8x7b has weird max_pos handling in the checkpoint metadata.
meera: can you dump model.config max_position_embeddings and RoPE table size?
jordan: model.config.max_position_embeddings=2048, but we serve with dynamic sliding-window and our offset arithmetic allowed abs_pos up to ~4096 which trips pos_wrap guard.
sam: aha. chooser defensively avoids fast kernel if abs_pos > max_pos to avoid OOB. so two options: clamp abs_pos or relax guard when we have wrap-safe KV addressing.
meera: relaxing guard seems risky. For short term we can clamp virtual positions via prefix normalization in runtime.
carla: also check kv tile alignment: when seq slightly > max_pos our tile calculator flips tiling stride which triggers fallback.
jordan: quick experiment: clamped positions -> kernel stays matmul_fp16_fast and latency returns to baseline. patch diff:
```
- abs_pos = start_pos + i
+ abs_pos = min(start_pos + i, model.max_pos - 1)
```
ops-bot: deploy_bot: referenced PR #4892 to runtime:clamp-pos-preload (staging)
sam: good. but we should add a unit test for tiling logic + a chooser test vector where max_pos < running_abs_pos.
meera: agree. also we need a perf guard for batching heuristics: with clamping, large batches (batch>4) still sometimes pick the generic kernel due to memory tile estimate. We should expose a config knob to favor latency over memory for dedicated customers.
carla: logging suggestion: include chooser_debug_id and tile_estimates in traces so we can correlate traces->latency regressions. small JSON sample:
```
{ "chooser_id": "c123", "tile_bytes": 24MB, "fast_kernel_estimate": 18MB, "selected": "generic" }
```
jordan: I'll open an RFC for: 1) clamp positions for sliding-window when model.max_pos < computed abs_pos 2) add chooser unit tests 3) add config knob prefer_low_latency 4) emit chooser debug in traces.
meera: also add a benchmark matrix for Mistral-7B and Mistral-8x7B with seq=2k..6k in CI (small matrix, perf job) so we catch this earlier.
sam: noted. for rollout plan: patch -> staging smoke perf -> canary with prefer_low_latency=false -> enable for a small dedicated customer.
jordan: ok i pushed the runtime patch to staging, leaving the canary toggle off. will post perf numbers in the morning.
carla: thanks. would be good to add a short doc blurb in eng-runtime about RoPE/poswrap pitfalls for model onboards.
meera: +1. thanks all.
